git-governance.description: Git branch and repository governance semantics.

operations-core.description: Cross-domain operational identity and observation semantics.

transition-protocol.description: Verifiable mutation plan and receipt semantics.

artifact.receipt.definition: Evidence emitted only after a mutation is applied and verified by readback.

artifact.recommendation.definition: Read-only policy interpretation that does not itself authorize mutation.

artifact.routing-plan.definition: Read-only routing decision without transport side effects.

artifact.sanitization-plan.definition: Plan describing potentially destructive maintenance; execution requires a separate guarded executor.

artifact.transition-plan.definition: Deterministic mutation candidate bound to before-state and exact plan identity.

branch.class.authority.definition: Branch class reserved for an explicitly declared live authority; the name alone never grants authority.

branch.class.experiment.definition: Branch class for bounded experimental work; the name does not imply retention or promotion.

branch.class.work.definition: Branch class for transient implementation work; the name does not imply deletion eligibility.

capability.policy.definition: Current capability policy vocabulary: experimental, canonical, deprecated, disabled.

coordination.lease.definition: Temporary exclusive write ownership over an exact coordination resource.

core.authority.definition: Canonical source for a mutable operational fact within a domain.

core.canonical-writer.definition: The single supported mutation surface for one mutable authority.

core.projection.definition: Derived representation that never becomes an independent source of truth.

identity.role.definition: Logical function fulfilled by one or more workers.

identity.session.definition: Ephemeral execution instance of a worker.

identity.worker.definition: Persistent identifiable executor of a logical role.

identity.worker-reference.definition: Reference to a worker identity from another operational contract.

status.observation.definition: Epistemic observation status: PASS means required facts were observed and validated; UNKNOWN means they could not be determined; FAIL means required factual observation or contract validation failed.
